readings: head at +x: XY panel is the profile, ZY is the front view, XZ is the top view
XY: nose (24,7), ear-base/head-top (20,3), withers (16,8), mid-back (12,8), hip/rump (8,11), tail-base (8,11), tail-tip (1,8)
XY: front shoulder (15,9), front knee (14,15), front paw (14,20)
XY: hind hip (9,13), hind knee (8,17), hind paw (9,20)
ground line at y=20-21 in XY panel, so leg lengths = shoulder(9)->paw(20) and hip(13)->paw(20)
ZY panel confirms two front legs at different z (one straight z~8, one bent z~13-15) and ear tips near z=10-14,y=2-3, used only to set left/right z-offsets, not lengths

notes: Head at +x in the XY panel identifies it as the profile view; ZY is the front (facing) view and XZ is the top view. Spine chain (spine_root=hip region -> withers -> neck -> head) and tail were read directly from XY-panel landmarks. Front and hind legs were each split into a proximal segment (shoulder/hip) and two limb segments (upper+lower) based on the visible knee bend in the XY panel; the small lateral (z) offset used to separate left/right legs at the shoulder/hip joints was inferred from the ZY (front) panel, since the XY profile only shows one leg silhouette per pair. All four legs and both front paws/hind paws were authored with equal proportional lengths despite the mid-stride pose shown (one front leg bent, one straight) per the proportion-not-pose rule. XZ (top) panel did not add usable limb data since legs are hidden under the body outline from above; it was used only to confirm head/tail placement along x.
